children.blurb: Ethics review with AI assistance covers the use of machine learning and natural language tools to support institutional review boards, research ethics committees, and integrity offices as they assess human subjects research, data protection, conflicts of interest, and publication ethics.

children.blurb: Provenance of research images and data is the record of where a dataset or image came from, how it was created or collected, who modified it, and under what conditions it can be reused.

sections.body: This field covers the rules, roles and records that keep research trustworthy when artificial intelligence is part of the work. In practice, AI is used to screen manuscripts for fabricated citations, compare images for signs of duplication or editing, summarize ethics protocols and help draft disclosure statements. It also introduces new failure modes, including invented references, unclear authorship contributions, training data drawn from copyrighted or sensitive sources and images that no longer match the underlying data. The central question is not whether AI can write or check text, but who is responsible for the claims that reach publication. Governance here means disclosure, verification, review and the ability to trace a result back to its evidence.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are partly solved, such as flagging obviously broken citations or comparing an image against its own metadata. Other tasks remain hard, including proving that a training corpus was lawfully assembled, detecting subtle image manipulation and deciding when AI assistance in ethics review must be disclosed. Authorship rules are still uneven across journals and institutions, and many policies do not say how much AI use is acceptable or how it should be credited. AI detectors are unreliable, provenance metadata is often missing and review boards rarely have the time or expertise to audit every claim. The site's library of 135 research papers is one sample of this literature, and it shows several competing approaches rather than one settled standard. The honest limit is that governance often runs behind the tools it tries to govern.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader concerned with credit and accountability should start with AI and Authorship, which examines who or what counts as an author and how contributions are disclosed. Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking follows the verification chain, showing how invented references are caught and why checking remains partly manual. Training Data and Academic Work looks upstream at the corpora that feed models and the copyright, consent and attribution questions they raise. Ethics Review with AI Assistance turns to the review process itself, including where AI can help screen protocols and where human judgment must remain. Provenance of Research Images and Data closes the loop by asking how images, datasets and results can be traced to their origins. Together these pages move from authorship to evidence to review to provenance, and each one can be read alone or as part of the larger section.
